claim: Let \(X\) be a nonempty noncontractible finite \(T_0\)-space and let \(D_n\) be the discrete \(n\)-point finite space. For every integer \(n\ge 2\), if \(Z=X\oplus D_n\) is the non-Hausdorff join obtained by placing every point of \(X\) below every point of \(D_n\), then, in the unreduced Schwarz-genus convention, \(\mathrm{TC}(Z)=n^2\).
integrity: The universal statement is proved symbolically. Finite computation only checks the retraction and maximal-pair mechanism on representative sample bases and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The base finite space must be nonempty and noncontractible; for a contractible base the join is contractible and has topological complexity 1.
The upper factor is required to be discrete, so the theorem does not cover arbitrary finite ordinal sums.
The theorem determines the exact number of motion-planning domains but does not classify optimal sections.
title: Quadratic topological complexity after adjoining maximal antichains
